title.sl: Poudarek: it was … who, what … is, do
title.de: Hervorheben: it was … who, what … is, do
title.it: Mettere in rilievo: it was … who, what … is, do
title.en: Emphasis: it was … who, what … is, do

rule.sl:
**It was** + kar je pomembno + **who** (oseba) ali **that** (kar koli): **It was Jack who found her.** **It was the fog that stopped him.** **It was in Keswick that we met.** Ostane ednina: **It was Jack and Meg who found her.** Tudi v sedanjiku: **It's the cold that I hate.** Ljudje rečejo tudi *It was Jack what found her*; v pisanju who.

**What** + stavek + **is**, **was**: kar je pomembno, pride zadnje. **What I need is a rest.** **What she needed was a cup of tea.** Za dejanje **did was** + osnovna oblika: **What Jack did was ring the inn.** **All I want is a quiet night.** Pred is ni vejice.

**do, does, did** + osnovna oblika, izgovorjeno močno, kadar kdo dvomi: **I do like your soup.** **She did ring, twice.** Prijazno: **Do sit down.**

Prepoznaj v zgodbah in govorih: za **Never**, **Rarely**, **Not only** stoji pomožni glagol pred osebkom, kot v vprašanju. **Never have I seen such fog.** = **I have never seen such fog.** **Not only did she get lost, but she also lost a shoe.**
rule.de:
**It was** + das Wichtige + **who** (eine Person) oder **that** (alles): **It was Jack who found her.** **It was the fog that stopped him.** **It was in Keswick that we met.** Es bleibt Singular: **It was Jack and Meg who found her.** Auch im Präsens: **It's the cold that I hate.** Man sagt auch *It was Jack what found her*; geschrieben who.

**What** + Satz + **is**, **was**: das Wichtige kommt zuletzt. **What I need is a rest.** **What she needed was a cup of tea.** Für eine Handlung **did was** + Grundform: **What Jack did was ring the inn.** **All I want is a quiet night.** Vor is kein Komma.

**do, does, did** + Grundform, betont gesprochen, wenn jemand zweifelt: **I do like your soup.** **She did ring, twice.** Herzlich: **Do sit down.**

Zum Erkennen, in Geschichten und Reden: Nach **Never**, **Rarely**, **Not only** steht das Hilfsverb vor dem Subjekt, wie in einer Frage. **Never have I seen such fog.** = **I have never seen such fog.** **Not only did she get lost, but she also lost a shoe.**
rule.it:
**It was** + ciò che conta + **who** (una persona) o **that** (qualsiasi cosa): **It was Jack who found her.** **It was the fog that stopped him.** **It was in Keswick that we met.** Resta al singolare: **It was Jack and Meg who found her.** Anche al presente: **It's the cold that I hate.** Si dice anche *It was Jack what found her*; per iscritto who.

**What** + frase + **is**, **was**: ciò che conta viene per ultimo. **What I need is a rest.** **What she needed was a cup of tea.** Per un'azione **did was** + forma base: **What Jack did was ring the inn.** **All I want is a quiet night.** Niente virgola prima di is.

**do, does, did** + forma base, pronunciato con enfasi, quando qualcuno dubita: **I do like your soup.** **She did ring, twice.** Con calore: **Do sit down.**

Da riconoscere, nei racconti e nei discorsi: dopo **Never**, **Rarely**, **Not only** l'ausiliare viene prima del soggetto, come in una domanda. **Never have I seen such fog.** = **I have never seen such fog.** **Not only did she get lost, but she also lost a shoe.**
rule.en:
**It was** + what matters + **who** (a person) or **that** (anything): **It was Jack who found her.** **It was the fog that stopped him.** **It was in Keswick that we met.** It stays singular: **It was Jack and Meg who found her.** In the present too: **It's the cold that I hate.** People also say *It was Jack what found her*; writing wants who.

**What** + a clause + **is**, **was**: what matters comes last. **What I need is a rest.** **What she needed was a cup of tea.** For an action **did was** + the base form: **What Jack did was ring the inn.** **All I want is a quiet night.** No comma before is.

**do, does, did** + the base form, said with weight, when someone doubts it: **I do like your soup.** **She did ring, twice.** Warmly: **Do sit down.**

To recognise, in stories and speeches: after **Never**, **Rarely**, **Not only** the helping verb comes before the subject, as in a question. **Never have I seen such fog.** = **I have never seen such fog.** **Not only did she get lost, but she also lost a shoe.**

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina poudarja z besednim redom (*Našel jo je Jack*), angleščina z **It was Jack who found her.**
tip.de: 💡 *Was ich brauche, ist …* hat ein Komma, **What I need is …** keins. Und *Es waren Jack und Meg* heißt **It was Jack and Meg.**
tip.it: 💡 *È stato Jack a trovarla*: in inglese **It was Jack who found her**, sempre con it e sempre **was**.
tip.en: 💡 **It was** stays singular, and **did** takes the base form: **She did ring.**
